chunks: And Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who said:

to a woman, 'O adulteress,' and she replied, 'You are more adulterous than me.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The legal punishment (hadd) is upon her for what she accused him of. As for her self-admission, she is not to be punished unless she confesses to that before the Imam four times.'

key_terms.الْحَدُّ: The legal punishment (specifically for qadhf or zina)
key_terms.قَذَفَتْهُ بِهِ: She accused him of (specifically of adultery)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a woman's self-admission of adultery to be valid for legal punishment in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the hadd punishment for qadhf (false accusation) and the conditions for hadd al-zina, ruling that the woman is punished for accusing the man but her own admission of adultery requires four explicit confessions before the Imam to be valid. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the Imam's authority in validating confessions for major punishments, ensuring procedural rigor beyond mere verbal admission. It underscores the principle that while qadhf is immediate upon accusation, the penalty for zina based on self-incrimination demands a higher threshold of clarity and presence of the judge.
